verdict: The real Library and Wishlist already inherit the new Intercom-style shell, but their internal hierarchy still reads as a lightly restyled media gallery and generic card page rather than the reference product's dense operational workspaces.
differences: Library controls are scattered across a search band, small floating filter buttons and a separate heading instead of one coherent workspace header and filter strip.
The default poster grid leaves a large unstructured canvas and gives status less prominence than the Intercom content and contacts rows.
Library list rows and preview inspector are functional but use tighter, sharper geometry than the reference's 10-14px control/card radii and 40-44px targets.
Wishlist uses separate pill groups and card-like rows; the approved Inbox pattern uses a compact tab/filter header, divider-led queue rows and a stable selected-item inspector.
Wishlist's empty state is serviceable but lacks the reference system's pane title, result count and bounded operational context.
Selection currently relies on a left accent and semantic color while the reference uses a quiet neutral or pale-blue well with a fine border and soft elevation.
Primary actions and status controls need clearer charcoal-versus-semantic hierarchy and more consistent alignment on the trailing edge.
suggestions: Unify each route under a compact workspace header with title, description/count, search, filters and actions aligned to a 4px rhythm.
Make Library list mode the Intercom-like operational view while retaining the existing poster toggle and every current filter, sort and preview behavior.
Restyle poster cards with bounded media, stable metadata and status regions rather than adding decorative overlays.
Turn Wishlist into an Inbox-like queue: compact category/status controls, divider-led rows and a sticky inspector on wide screens.
Use only existing HolyArrs data and actions; preserve permission checks, approval dialogs, request states, retry states and direct media links.
Keep tablet and mobile drill-in behavior and 44px coarse-pointer targets because the reference corpus is desktop-only.
reasoning: Compared at the live 18746 desktop viewport against the approved exported Intercom references, especially 160.png and 400.png. The shell and palette now carry much of the reference character, but these two page bodies need the denser shared-row hierarchy, calm neutral selection, bounded inspector and consolidated controls that make Intercom feel operational rather than gallery-like. Exact motion is not scored because the available evidence is still imagery rather than a verified recording.
